settings.name_in_paper: Contextual K-armed bandit with neural-network (NTK) reward approximation
unmapped: Reward r_{t,k} = h(x_{t,k}) + xi_{t,k} with unknown bounded function h (|h|<=1); complexity measured through the neural tangent kernel matrix H on the TK observed contexts and effective dimension d_tilde
NTK matrix assumed positive definite: H >= lambda_0 I (Assumption 4)
Contexts have unit norm and symmetric structure [x]_j = [x]_{j+d/2}
Each round K context vectors (one per arm) are revealed; the set of all TK contexts is treated as fixed for the analysis
Exploration variance nu requires knowledge of B = max{1/(22 e sqrt(pi)), sqrt(2 h^T H^{-1} h)} (an NTK-RKHS norm bound) and of d_tilde
settings.definition_quote: In this work, we consider contextual $K$-armed bandits, where the total number of rounds $T$ is known. At round $t \in [T]$, the agent observes $K$ contextual vectors $\{\xb_{t, k} \in \RR^d~|~ k \in [K]\}$. ... $r_{t, k} = h(\xb_{t, k}) + \xi_{t, k}$, with $|h(\xb_{t, k})| \le 1$ where $\{\xi_{t, k}\}$ forms an $R$-sub-Gaussian martingale difference sequence

bound.expression_latex: R_T \le C_3(1 + c_T)\nu\sqrt{2\lambda L(\tilde d\log(1 + TK) + 1)T} + (4 + C_4(1 + c_T)\nu L)\sqrt{2\log(3 /\delta) T} + 5
bound.regime: network width m >= poly(lambda, T, K, L, log(1/delta), 1/lambda_0)

symbols.d_tilde: effective dimension log det(I + H/lambda)/log(1 + TK/lambda) of the NTK matrix H

conditions: Assumption 4: NTK matrix H >= lambda_0 I with lambda_0 > 0
network width m satisfies Condition 10 (polynomial in T, K, L, log(1/delta), 1/lambda_0)
tuning: nu = B + R*sqrt(d_tilde*log(1+TK/lambda) + 2 + 2*log(1/delta)), B = max{1/(22 e sqrt(pi)), sqrt(2 h^T H^{-1} h)}
eta = C_1 (m lambda + m L T)^{-1}
J = (1 + LT/lambda)(C_2 + log(T^3 L lambda^{-1} log(1/delta)))/C_1 gradient descent iterations

source.label: thm:main
source.quote:
Under Assumption ef{assumption:input}, set the parameters in Algorithm ef{alg:main} as $\lambda = 1 + 1 / T$, $
u = B + R\sqrt{	ilde d \log(1 + TK/\lambda) + 2 + 2\log (1 / \delta)}$ ... If the network width $m$ satisfies: $m \ge \mathrm{poly}(\lambda, T, K, L, \log(1 / \delta), \lambda_0^{-1})$, then, with probability at least $1 - \delta$, the regret of Algorithm ef{alg:main} is bounded as $R_T \le C_3(1 + c_T)
u\sqrt{2\lambda L(	ilde d\log(1 + TK) + 1)T} + (4 + C_4(1 + c_T)
u L)\sqrt{2\log(3 /\delta) T} + 5$, where $C_3, C_4$ are some positive absolute constants, and $c_T = \sqrt{4\log T + 2\log K}$.

results.notes: R_T is defined as an expectation of the regret against the per-round best arm, but the theorem bounds it with probability 1-delta (over network initialisation etc.); recorded as high-probability. Remark 7 summarises the bound as O~(d_tilde sqrt(T)). Remark 9 states a doubling trick gives similar regret for unknown T (informal, not recorded). Action space mapped to kernel_rkhs because complexity is via the NTK; the reward function is only assumed bounded, with B measuring its NTK-RKHS norm. Environment set stochastic_iid with contexts as an oblivious sequence.
